patches.before: She stared at me. I decided not to die over vocabulary.
patches.after: Octavia held my gaze for one beat, then reopened the ledger. I decided not to die over vocabulary.
patches.reason: FREE rehearsal keeps Octavia's pressure inside the work. She does not need a generic stare when returning to the ledger makes the social boundary and task ownership visible at once.

patches.before:
She frowned.

“Why do you like whatever it is you do?”
patches.after:
Octavia stopped writing long enough to frown at me.

“Why do you like whatever it is you do?”
patches.reason: Her curiosity lands harder when it visibly interrupts work rather than appearing as generic facial description.

patches.before:
Ressa looked at him.

“Can you?”

“Yes.”

“Then stop it if shouting fails.”
patches.after:
Ressa pointed the broken pencil at him.

“Can you?”

“Yes.”

“Shout first. If that fails, stop it.”
patches.reason: Ressa's dialogue becomes more procedural and her movement keeps her authority attached to the intake work rather than a generic look.

patches.after:
Ressa tapped the broken pencil against the intake sheet.

“Guild training?”

“Yes.”

“Of course.”
patches.reason: The same line reads more specifically as Ressa when her skepticism stays embedded in the intake process.

patches.after:
The mage shifted between me and the body.

“Why?”
patches.reason: Kellan's first boundary is access to evidence. Blocking Greg from the body is more character- and pressure-specific than a generic crossed-arms beat.

patches.before:
He looked surprised. I started to leave.

“Wait.”

I stopped. He pointed at my wrist.
patches.after:
I started to leave. His eyes dropped to my wrist tag.

“Wait.”

I stopped. He pointed at my wrist.
patches.reason: The turn is not generic surprise; Greg's casting restriction is the concrete detail that makes Kellan reconsider access.

patches.before:
“Was that you making me better?”

“No.”

He looked surprised.

“That was you.”

He was quiet. Good. Let him own it. Then he ruined the moment.

“You still owe me a scarf.”
patches.after:
“Was that you making me better?”

“No.”

Alden looked down at the grass in his hand.

“That was you.”

He rolled the stems between his fingers. Good. Let him own it.

Then he looked at the red strip around his wrist.

“You still owe me a scarf.”
patches.reason: The relationship beat benefits from embodied silence: Alden gets a moment to absorb ownership of his own competence, then the scarf physically routes him back into their familiar argument.
